_help: Each frame is one page of the guide, shown above its step's text; Back / Next turn the pages. A frame's picture is assets/excelcomputer/textures/gui/guide/<image>.png, any size (640x360 looks sharp). Until it exists, the guide shows the 'shot' note instead.

steps.text: Craft an Excel Table from planks and paper, place it and right-click it to open your workbooks.

frames.shot: A crafting table GUI with the Excel Table recipe in the grid and the Excel Table in the result slot.
In the world: the player looking at a placed Excel Table, about to right-click it.

steps.text: Put an Excel Table at the top of a diagonal line of 2 sticks to make Excel on a Stick. Use it anywhere to open your workbooks without the table.

frames.shot: Crafting grid: Excel Table in the top right, 2 sticks going diagonally down to the bottom left, Excel on a Stick in the result slot.
First person, holding Excel on a Stick in the hand (outdoors, nothing else in view).

steps.text: The picker lists the .xlsx and .csv files in your workbooks folder. Click one to open it, or press Open folder to add your own files, then Refresh.

frames.shot: The workbook picker screen with 3-4 workbooks listed.
The Windows File Explorer window of the workbooks folder (.minecraft/excelcomputer/workbooks) with a few .xlsx files.

steps.text: Craft an Excel Guide (Excel Paper on top of a book) to read this guide anytime. You can also hold W over any Excel item in your inventory.

frames.shot: Crafting grid: Excel Paper above a book, the Excel Guide in the result slot.
An inventory with the mouse over Excel on a Stick, tooltip showing "Hold [W] for the guide" with the bar half full.

steps.text: Click a cell and type. Enter confirms, the arrow keys move. Formulas start with =, like =SUM(A1:A5).

frames.shot: A spreadsheet with a few numbers in column A and cell A6 selected.
The same sheet while typing =SUM(A1:A5) into A6 (formula bar showing it).
The same sheet after Enter: A6 shows the total.

steps.text: While you type a formula, matching functions pop up: Tab picks one. The fx button next to the formula bar lists every function.

frames.shot: Typing =SU in a cell, with the autocomplete list open below it.
The function menu opened from the fx button.

steps.text: The Home tab formats cells: fonts, colors, borders, number formats, alignment and conditional formatting. Right-click cells for a quick menu.

frames.shot: The ribbon's Home tab, with a range of cells selected and some of them colored or bold.
The right-click menu (and mini toolbar) open over a selected cell.

steps.text: Press Ctrl+S to save. If you leave with unsaved changes, the status line warns you once first.

frames.shot: The spreadsheet's status line after saving ("Saved ...").

steps.text: Craft Excel Paper from paper and green dye. In the picker, press Share... and click a workbook: it becomes an item you can hand to anyone (uses 1 Excel Paper).

frames.shot: Crafting grid: paper in the middle, 8 green dye around it, Excel Paper in the result slot.
The picker after pressing Share...: the workbooks read "Share <name>".
The new Shared Workbook item in the hotbar with its tooltip showing.

steps.text: Right-click the item to open it. Your saves update it for everyone; other players' saves go to a copy in their own workbooks. Shared workbooks expire after 7 days.

frames.shot: A second player with the shared workbook open (status line: "Shared by ...").

steps.text: My shared sheets (top right of the picker) lists what you shared, when each one expires, and lets you delete them.

frames.shot: The My shared sheets screen with 2-3 entries.

steps.text: A Logistics Hub moves items between inventories the way its workbook says. Craft one from an Excel Table, an ender pearl and copper, iron, diamonds or netherite.

frames.shot: Crafting grid: 7 copper ingots around an Excel Table, ender pearl top middle, Copper Logistics Hub as the result.
The four hubs placed in a row: Copper, Iron, Diamond, Netherite.

steps.text: Better hubs reach farther, move more items more often and hold more inventories. Only a Netherite hub reaches other dimensions. Each hub's workbook says what it can do. To upgrade a hub without losing its workbook or inventories, right-click it with the next tier's Hub Upgrade.

frames.shot: Right-clicking a Copper Logistics Hub while holding an Iron Hub Upgrade, the action bar saying "Upgraded. Iron Logistics Hub: ...".
The hub's workbook just opened, showing the Inventories sheet with its notes on the right ("This hub: ... moves up to ...") and the sheet tabs (Inventories, Stock, Transfers).

steps.text: Right-click a hub to open its workbook. It also becomes your active hub: the one new inventories join.

frames.shot: In the world: right-clicking a hub, the action bar says "... selected (0/4 inventories)".
The hub's workbook just opened, showing the Inventories sheet with its notes on the right ("This hub: ... moves up to ...") and the sheet tabs (Inventories, Stock, Transfers).

steps.text: Open your hubs from anywhere: choose one in the picker's hub dropdown and press Open, or sneak and use Excel on a Stick in the air.

frames.shot: The picker's hub row with the dropdown open, listing 2-3 named hubs.
First person, sneaking with Excel on a Stick in hand, far away from any hub.

steps.text: Hold Excel on a Stick, sneak and right-click the side of a chest, furnace, barrel or modded storage. It joins your active hub. Do it again to take it off. A storage controller (like Sophisticated Storage's) adds its whole storage network as one inventory. Tanks work the same way, for moving fluids.

frames.shot: Sneaking and right-clicking the side of a chest with the stick.
The action bar right after: "Added Chest 1 (North side) to ...".
Sneak-clicking the same chest again: "Removed Chest 1 from ...".

steps.text: The side you click is where items go in: a furnace's top smelts, its side takes fuel. Click more sides of the same block to use them too ("Furnace 1 Top").

frames.shot: Sneak-clicking the TOP of a furnace.
Sneak-clicking the SIDE of the same furnace.
Sneak-clicking the BOTTOM of the same furnace (looking up at it).

steps.text: The Inventories sheet lists them with their status. Change a Name or Side and save to update it; delete a row and save to remove that inventory.

frames.shot: The Inventories sheet with a chest and a furnace (3 sides) listed, all with Status OK.

steps.text: Every cycle, each row of the Transfers sheet moves items From one inventory To another. Item says which items, Amount how many. Status tells you what happened. For fluids, write fluid: in front (fluid:water, fluid:*) and give Amount in millibuckets: 1000 is a bucket.

frames.shot: The Transfers sheet with 2-3 filled rows and their Status column ("Moved 8", "Nothing to move").

steps.text: Item can be an id (minecraft:coal), a tag (#c:ingots), a wildcard (*_ingot) or * for anything. Separate several with commas; ! in front leaves items out.

frames.shot: Close-up of the Item column with examples: minecraft:coal, #c:ingots, *_ingot, "*, !minecraft:dirt".

steps.text: The Stock sheet shows what every inventory holds. Use it in formulas: Amount =MAX(0, 16-SUMIFS(StockCount, StockInventory, "Furnace 1", StockItem, "minecraft:coal")) keeps 16 coal in Furnace 1.

frames.shot: The Stock sheet with a few inventories and items listed.
A Transfers row whose Amount cell is selected, the SUMIFS formula visible in the formula bar.

steps.text: Example smelter: Chest 1 to Furnace 1 Top (*ore), Chest 1 to Furnace 1 East, a side (coal), Furnace 1 Bottom to Chest 1 (*ingot).

frames.shot: In the world: a hub, a chest and a furnace next to each other.
The Transfers sheet with exactly those 3 rows filled in.
The chest opened afterwards, with iron ingots in it.

steps.text: Whoever places a hub owns it. In the picker, press Access next to the hub and type a player's name (they must be online). Members can open the workbook and add inventories.

frames.shot: The picker's hub row, with the mouse over the Access button.
The Access panel with one member added (name + Remove button).

steps.text: Only one player edits a hub's workbook at a time; others are told who is editing. Only the owner can rename the hub, change who has access or break it.

frames.shot: A second player trying to open the hub: "<name> is editing this Logistics Hub right now".
